key: Noah and the Big Boat. Long ago there was a man named Noah. God loved Noah, and Noah loved God.
say: Noah and the Big Boat. Long ago there was a man named Noah. God loved Noah, and Noah loved God.

key: God told Noah, "A big flood is coming. Build a great big boat called an ark!" Noah trusted God, so he listened and obeyed. Bang, bang, bang!
say: God told Noah, "A big flood is coming. Build a great big boat called an ark!" Noah trusted God, so he listened and obeyed. Bang, bang, bang!

key: Noah's three sons helped him build. They sawed the wood and carried big, long boards. Everyone worked hard, day after day.
say: Noah's three sons helped him build. They sawed the wood and carried big, long boards. Everyone worked hard, day after day.

key: God said, "Bring food for your family and for the animals, too." So they carried in baskets of fruit, sacks of grain, and lots and lots of hay!
say: God said, "Bring food for your family and for the animals, too." So they carried in baskets of fruit, sacks of grain, and lots and lots of hay!

key: At last, the ark was almost ready. It was big and strong, with a roof, windows, and a door, just like God said.
say: At last, the ark was almost ready. It was big and strong, with a roof, windows, and a door, just like God said.

key: Safe in the Ark. Noah's family built the big ark, just like God said. Then God said, "It is time. Go into the ark, with your family and the animals."
say: Safe in the Ark. Noah's family built the big ark, just like God said. Then God said, "It is time. Go into the ark, with your family and the animals."

key: Then the animals came, two by two! Lions and elephants and giraffes, too.
say: Then the animals came, two by two! Lions and elephants and giraffes, too.

key: The rain fell and fell. But Noah, his family, and all the animals were safe inside the ark. God kept them safe.
say: The rain fell and fell. But Noah, his family, and all the animals were safe inside the ark. God kept them safe.

key: It rained for forty days and forty nights. Inside the ark, Noah's family fed the animals and took good care of them.
say: It rained for forty days and forty nights. Inside the ark, Noah's family fed the animals and took good care of them.

key: When the rain stopped, the water went down, down, down. Noah sent out a little dove. The dove came back with an olive leaf! There was dry land again.
say: When the rain stopped, the water went down, down, down. Noah sent out a little dove. The dove came back with an olive leaf! There was dry land again.

key: God put a beautiful rainbow in the sky. It was His promise: He would never flood the whole earth again. And God always keeps His promises!
say: God put a beautiful rainbow in the sky. It was His promise: He would never flood the whole earth again. And God always keeps His promises!

key: I set my rainbow in the cloud. Genesis 9:13.
say: I set my rainbow in the cloud. Genesis nine, thirteen.

key: God Made Everything. In the very beginning, there was only God. On day one, God said, let there be light! And there was light. And God saw that it was good!
say: God Made Everything. In the very beginning, there was only God. On day one, God said, let there be light! And there was light. And God saw that it was good!

key: On day two, God made the big blue sky up high, and the splashy sea down low.
say: On day two, God made the big blue sky up high, and the splashy sea down low.

key: On day three, God made dry land, with tall trees, soft grass, and pretty flowers. And God saw that it was good!
say: On day three, God made dry land, with tall trees, soft grass, and pretty flowers. And God saw that it was good!

key: On day four, God made the bright sun for the daytime, and the moon and twinkly stars for the night. And God saw that it was good!
say: On day four, God made the bright sun for the daytime, and the moon and twinkly stars for the night. And God saw that it was good!

key: On day five, God filled the sea with fish, and the sky with birds. Splish, splash! Tweet, tweet! And God saw that it was good!
say: On day five, God filled the sea with fish, and the sky with birds. Splish, splash! Tweet, tweet! And God saw that it was good!

key: On day six, God made animals of every kind. And God saw that it was good!
say: On day six, God made animals of every kind. And God saw that it was good!

key: God's Special Friends. On day six, after God made the animals, He made the first people, Adam and Eve! God loved them, and He made them to be His friends.
say: God's Special Friends. On day six, after God made the animals, He made the first people, Adam and Eve! God loved them, and He made them to be His friends.

key: God gave Adam and Eve a beautiful garden called Eden. It had a sparkly river and trees full of yummy fruit. God asked them to take good care of it.
say: God gave Adam and Eve a beautiful garden called Eden. It had a sparkly river and trees full of yummy fruit. God asked them to take good care of it.

key: God brought the animals to Adam, and Adam gave each one a name. Zebra! Monkey! Bear! What a fun job!
say: God brought the animals to Adam, and Adam gave each one a name. Zebra! Monkey! Bear! What a fun job!

key: God looked at everything He made, and it was very, very good! Then, on day seven, God rested, because all His work was done. God made it all, and God made you, too!
say: God looked at everything He made, and it was very, very good! Then, on day seven, God rested, because all His work was done. God made it all, and God made you, too!

key: Yes, you! God made your eyes to see, your ears to hear, and your hands to clap. You are wonderfully made, and God loves you so much!
say: Yes, you! God made your eyes to see, your ears to hear, and your hands to clap. You are wonderfully made, and God loves you so much!

key: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. Genesis 1:1.
say: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. Genesis one, one.

key: David and the Giant. David was a shepherd boy who took care of his sheep. God loved David, and David loved God.
say: David and the Giant. David was a shepherd boy who took care of his sheep. God loved David, and David loved God.

key: Every day, David led his father's sheep to green grass and cool water. When a little lamb got tired, David carried it in his arms.
say: Every day, David led his father's sheep to green grass and cool water. When a little lamb got tired, David carried it in his arms.

key: Out in the fields, David sang songs to God. God helped David keep his sheep safe, even from a lion and a bear!
say: Out in the fields, David sang songs to God. God helped David keep his sheep safe, even from a lion and a bear!

key: Remember Samuel, who listened to God? Now Samuel was old, and God sent him to David's family. David's big brothers were tall and strong. But God looks at the heart. God picked David to be king one day!
say: Remember Samuel, who listened to God? Now Samuel was old, and God sent him to David's family. David's big brothers were tall and strong. But God looks at the heart. God picked David to be king one day!

key: At night, under the twinkly stars, David played his harp. He made up songs for God. One song says, God is my shepherd. He takes care of me!
say: At night, under the twinkly stars, David played his harp. He made up songs for God. One song says, God is my shepherd. He takes care of me!

key: David Trusts God. Remember David, the shepherd boy who loved God? David's big brothers were soldiers in King Saul's army, far away.
say: David Trusts God. Remember David, the shepherd boy who loved God? David's big brothers were soldiers in King Saul's army, far away.

key: One day, David took some bread to his big brothers. A giant named Goliath was there. He was big and loud, and all the soldiers were afraid of him.
say: One day, David took some bread to his big brothers. A giant named Goliath was there. He was big and loud, and all the soldiers were afraid of him.

key: But David was not afraid. He told King Saul, "God helped me before, and God will help me now!" David trusted God.
say: But David was not afraid. He told King Saul, "God helped me before, and God will help me now!" David trusted God.

key: David went to a stream and picked five smooth stones. He put them in his shepherd's bag.
say: David went to a stream and picked five smooth stones. He put them in his shepherd's bag.

key: David swung his sling, round and round. Whoosh! The little stone flew, and the great big giant fell down. Boom!
say: David swung his sling, round and round. Whoosh! The little stone flew, and the great big giant fell down. Boom!

key: Everybody cheered! God helped David, just like David knew He would. God is bigger than any giant, and He is always with you, too!
say: Everybody cheered! God helped David, just like David knew He would. God is bigger than any giant, and He is always with you, too!

key: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you. Psalm 56:3.
say: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you. Psalm fifty-six, three.

key: Jonah and the Big Fish. God said to Jonah, go to the big city of Nineveh. Tell the people to stop doing wrong things and come back to Me.
say: Jonah and the Big Fish. God said to Jonah, go to the big city of Nineveh. Tell the people to stop doing wrong things and come back to Me.

key: But Jonah did not want to go! He ran the other way and got on a boat, sailing far, far away.
say: But Jonah did not want to go! He ran the other way and got on a boat, sailing far, far away.

key: Jonah went down inside the boat. He lay down and fell fast asleep.
say: Jonah went down inside the boat. He lay down and fell fast asleep.

key: God sent a big wind, and the boat rocked up and down. Jonah told the sailors, this storm is my fault. Put me into the sea. So they did. Splash! And the sea was calm again.
say: God sent a big wind, and the boat rocked up and down. Jonah told the sailors, this storm is my fault. Put me into the sea. So they did. Splash! And the sea was calm again.

key: But God sent a great big fish. Gulp! The fish swallowed Jonah up, and God kept him safe inside.
say: But God sent a great big fish. Gulp! The fish swallowed Jonah up, and God kept him safe inside.

key: A Second Chance. Remember Jonah? He ran away from God, and a big fish swallowed him up! But God was still with Jonah, even inside the fish.
say: A Second Chance. Remember Jonah? He ran away from God, and a big fish swallowed him up! But God was still with Jonah, even inside the fish.

key: Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights. He prayed to God and said, thank You for saving me!
say: Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights. He prayed to God and said, thank You for saving me!

key: Then God told the fish to spit Jonah out onto the dry land. Bleh! Jonah was back on the beach.
say: Then God told the fish to spit Jonah out onto the dry land. Bleh! Jonah was back on the beach.

key: God said to Jonah again, go to Nineveh and tell the people what I say. And Jonah said, yes, God! I will go.
say: God said to Jonah again, go to Nineveh and tell the people what I say. And Jonah said, yes, God! I will go.

key: God gave Jonah a second chance, and this time he went to Nineveh. The people listened, said sorry to God, and stopped doing wrong things. God forgave them, because God loves everyone!
say: God gave Jonah a second chance, and this time he went to Nineveh. The people listened, said sorry to God, and stopped doing wrong things. God forgave them, because God loves everyone!

key: And God gives second chances to you and me, too! When we say sorry, He forgives us. God loves us so much!
say: And God gives second chances to you and me, too! When we say sorry, He forgives us. God loves us so much!
God is love. First John four, eight.

key: Five Loaves and Two Fish. One day, a great big crowd came to see Jesus on a grassy hill. There were thousands and thousands of people!
say: Five Loaves and Two Fish. One day, a great big crowd came to see Jesus on a grassy hill. There were thousands and thousands of people!

key: Jesus told everyone how much God loves them. He made sick people well, too! All day long, He took care of them.
say: Jesus told everyone how much God loves them. He made sick people well, too! All day long, He took care of them.

key: It got late, and everyone was hungry. Grumble, grumble went their tummies! But where could they find food for so many people?
say: It got late, and everyone was hungry. Grumble, grumble went their tummies! But where could they find food for so many people?

key: Then a boy came with his lunch. He had five little loaves of bread and two little fish.
say: Then a boy came with his lunch. He had five little loaves of bread and two little fish.

key: The boy shared his lunch with Jesus. It was only a little bit of food. But Jesus knew just what to do!
say: The boy shared his lunch with Jesus. It was only a little bit of food. But Jesus knew just what to do!

key: Jesus held up the bread and fish and thanked God for the food. Then He passed it out to everyone.
say: Jesus held up the bread and fish and thanked God for the food. Then He passed it out to everyone.

key: More Than Enough. Remember the boy's little lunch? Jesus broke the bread, and His friends passed it out. More, and more, and more! The food never ran out.
say: More Than Enough. Remember the boy's little lunch? Jesus broke the bread, and His friends passed it out. More, and more, and more! The food never ran out.

key: Everyone ate and ate, until their tummies were full! There was plenty for everybody.
say: Everyone ate and ate, until their tummies were full! There was plenty for everybody.

key: There were even twelve baskets of leftovers! Jesus took one little lunch and made more than enough. Jesus cares for us and gives us what we need.
say: There were even twelve baskets of leftovers! Jesus took one little lunch and made more than enough. Jesus cares for us and gives us what we need.

key: Then the boy ran all the way home. "Mom! Dad! Jesus fed everybody with my little lunch!" What a happy day!
say: Then the boy ran all the way home. "Mom! Dad! Jesus fed everybody with my little lunch!" What a happy day!

key: The next day, Jesus said, "I am the bread of life." Bread fills our tummies, but Jesus fills our hearts! He takes care of us every single day.
say: The next day, Jesus said, "I am the bread of life." Bread fills our tummies, but Jesus fills our hearts! He takes care of us every single day.

key: Give us today our daily bread. Matthew 6:11.
say: Give us today our daily bread. Matthew six, eleven.

key: A Very Special Baby. Long ago, in a little town called Nazareth, there lived a young woman named Mary. One day, God sent an angel named Gabriel to visit her!
say: A Very Special Baby. Long ago, in a little town called Nazareth, there lived a young woman named Mary. One day, God sent an angel named Gabriel to visit her!

key: Gabriel said, "Don't be afraid, Mary! You will have a baby boy. He is God's own Son. Name Him Jesus!" Mary was so happy. She said yes to God!
say: Gabriel said, "Don't be afraid, Mary! You will have a baby boy. He is God's own Son. Name Him Jesus!" Mary was so happy. She said yes to God!

key: Mary was going to marry a kind man named Joseph. An angel came to Joseph in a dream, and told him all about the baby. Joseph trusted God, and took good care of Mary.
say: Mary was going to marry a kind man named Joseph. An angel came to Joseph in a dream, and told him all about the baby. Joseph trusted God, and took good care of Mary.

key: Mary and Joseph took a long trip to Bethlehem, King David's little town. Mary was going to have a very special baby!
say: Mary and Joseph took a long trip to Bethlehem, King David's little town. Mary was going to have a very special baby!

key: The town was so busy, there was no room for them to stay. So they stayed in a place where animals sleep.
say: The town was so busy, there was no room for them to stay. So they stayed in a place where animals sleep.

key: The First Christmas. One night, in the little stable, baby Jesus was born! Mary wrapped Him up snug and warm, and laid Him in a manger, where the animals eat their hay.
say: The First Christmas. One night, in the little stable, baby Jesus was born! Mary wrapped Him up snug and warm, and laid Him in a manger, where the animals eat their hay.

key: Out in the fields, shepherds were watching their sheep in the night.
say: Out in the fields, shepherds were watching their sheep in the night.

key: Suddenly, an angel came, and God's bright glory shone all around! The angel said, "Don't be afraid! I bring you good news of great joy for everyone!"
say: Suddenly, an angel came, and God's bright glory shone all around! The angel said, "Don't be afraid! I bring you good news of great joy for everyone!"

key: The angel said, "Today a Savior is born for you, Christ the Lord! You will find Him wrapped up snug, lying in a manger." Then lots and lots of angels sang, "Glory to God!"
say: The angel said, "Today a Savior is born for you, Christ the Lord! You will find Him wrapped up snug, lying in a manger." Then lots and lots of angels sang, "Glory to God!"

key: The shepherds hurried and found baby Jesus, just like the angel said! Jesus is God's best gift to us. He is our Savior, who came to rescue us, because God loves us so much.
say: The shepherds hurried and found baby Jesus, just like the angel said! Jesus is God's best gift to us. He is our Savior, who came to rescue us, because God loves us so much.

key: Later, wise men from far away followed a bright star all the way to Jesus. They brought Him wonderful gifts. Jesus is God's best gift, for the whole wide world!
say: Later, wise men from far away followed a bright star all the way to Jesus. They brought Him wonderful gifts. Jesus is God's best gift, for the whole wide world!

key: I bring you good news of great joy. Luke 2:10.
say: I bring you good news of great joy. Luke two, ten.

key: God's Big Promise. Long ago, a man named Abraham lived in a big, busy city with his wife, Sarah. God loved Abraham, and Abraham loved God.
say: God's Big Promise. Long ago, a man named Abraham lived in a big, busy city with his wife, Sarah. God loved Abraham, and Abraham loved God.

key: One day, God said, "Abraham, leave your home, and go to a new land. I will show you the way." Abraham did not know where he was going. But he trusted God!
say: One day, God said, "Abraham, leave your home, and go to a new land. I will show you the way." Abraham did not know where he was going. But he trusted God!

key: So Abraham and Sarah packed up their tents. They took their sheep and their camels, and off they went. They walked a long, long way!
say: So Abraham and Sarah packed up their tents. They took their sheep and their camels, and off they went. They walked a long, long way!

key: At last, they came to a beautiful land. God said, "I will give this land to your family." So Abraham and Sarah set up their tents, and they thanked God.
say: At last, they came to a beautiful land. God said, "I will give this land to your family." So Abraham and Sarah set up their tents, and they thanked God.

key: But Abraham and Sarah were very old, and they had no children. They wished for a baby so much.
say: But Abraham and Sarah were very old, and they had no children. They wished for a baby so much.

key: One night, God took Abraham outside and said, "Look up at the sky, and count the stars, if you can! Your family will be like the stars." And Abraham believed God.
say: One night, God took Abraham outside and said, "Look up at the sky, and count the stars, if you can! Your family will be like the stars." And Abraham believed God.

key: A Baby Named Laughter. Abraham and Sarah waited and waited, for years and years. Every night, Abraham looked up at the stars and remembered God's promise of a great big family.
say: A Baby Named Laughter. Abraham and Sarah waited and waited, for years and years. Every night, Abraham looked up at the stars and remembered God's promise of a great big family.

key: One hot day, three visitors came to Abraham's tent. Abraham ran to meet them. "Welcome!" he said. "Come and rest in the shade!"
say: One hot day, three visitors came to Abraham's tent. Abraham ran to meet them. "Welcome!" he said. "Come and rest in the shade!"

key: Sarah baked warm bread, and Abraham brought cool milk. The visitors sat under a big shady tree, and they ate and ate.
say: Sarah baked warm bread, and Abraham brought cool milk. The visitors sat under a big shady tree, and they ate and ate.

key: One visitor said, "Next year, Sarah will have a baby boy!" Sarah was listening at the tent door. She laughed and said, "Me? I am too old to have a baby!" But nothing is too hard for God.
say: One visitor said, "Next year, Sarah will have a baby boy!" Sarah was listening at the tent door. She laughed and said, "Me? I am too old to have a baby!" But nothing is too hard for God.

key: And God kept His promise! The next year, Sarah had a baby boy. They named him Isaac. Isaac means laughter! Sarah laughed for joy and said, "God has made me laugh!"
say: And God kept His promise! The next year, Sarah had a baby boy. They named him Isaac. Isaac means laughter! Sarah laughed for joy and said, "God has made me laugh!"

key: Abraham's family grew and grew, until it was like the stars in the sky! God always keeps His promises. And God's family has room for you, too!
say: Abraham's family grew and grew, until it was like the stars in the sky! God always keeps His promises. And God's family has room for you, too!

key: Look now toward the sky, and count the stars. Genesis 15:5.
say: Look now toward the sky, and count the stars. Genesis fifteen, five.

key: Joseph's Beautiful Coat. Long ago, a man named Jacob had twelve sons. He loved his son Joseph very, very much.
say: Joseph's Beautiful Coat. Long ago, a man named Jacob had twelve sons. He loved his son Joseph very, very much.

key: One day, Jacob gave Joseph a beautiful coat. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple!
say: One day, Jacob gave Joseph a beautiful coat. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple!

key: One night, Joseph had a dream. There were bundles of grain in a field. Joseph's bundle stood up tall, and his brothers' bundles all bowed down to it!
say: One night, Joseph had a dream. There were bundles of grain in a field. Joseph's bundle stood up tall, and his brothers' bundles all bowed down to it!

key: Joseph told his brothers all about his dream. But his brothers did not like it. They were jealous of Joseph and his beautiful coat. Grumble, grumble!
say: Joseph told his brothers all about his dream. But his brothers did not like it. They were jealous of Joseph and his beautiful coat. Grumble, grumble!

key: His brothers were so jealous that they took his coat. Then they sent Joseph far away, to a land called Egypt.
say: His brothers were so jealous that they took his coat. Then they sent Joseph far away, to a land called Egypt.

key: God Was With Joseph. Far away in Egypt, God was with Joseph. Joseph worked hard, and he was kind to everyone.
say: God Was With Joseph. Far away in Egypt, God was with Joseph. Joseph worked hard, and he was kind to everyone.

key: One night, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had a strange dream. Seven fat cows came up out of the river. Then seven skinny cows came up, too!
say: One night, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had a strange dream. Seven fat cows came up out of the river. Then seven skinny cows came up, too!

key: God helped Joseph explain the dream to Pharaoh. First there would be lots of food, like the fat cows. Then there would be no food, like the skinny cows.
say: God helped Joseph explain the dream to Pharaoh. First there would be lots of food, like the fat cows. Then there would be no food, like the skinny cows.

key: So Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all the food. Joseph saved up lots and lots of grain in big storehouses.
say: So Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all the food. Joseph saved up lots and lots of grain in big storehouses.

key: Soon there was no food anywhere, except in Joseph's storehouses! Joseph's hungry brothers came to Egypt to buy food. They bowed down low, just like in Joseph's dream! But they did not know it was Joseph.
say: Soon there was no food anywhere, except in Joseph's storehouses! Joseph's hungry brothers came to Egypt to buy food. They bowed down low, just like in Joseph's dream! But they did not know it was Joseph.

key: Joseph said, "I am Joseph, your brother!" He forgave his brothers, and they hugged and cried happy tears. God turned something bad into something good!
say: Joseph said, "I am Joseph, your brother!" He forgave his brothers, and they hugged and cried happy tears. God turned something bad into something good!

key: You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good. Genesis 50:20.
say: You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good. Genesis fifty, twenty.

key: Let My People Go. Remember Moses? He and his brother Aaron were on their way to Egypt. There, God's people were still making bricks for Pharaoh, the king, all day long. But God loved His people, and He had a plan.
say: Let My People Go. Remember Moses? He and his brother Aaron were on their way to Egypt. There, God's people were still making bricks for Pharaoh, the king, all day long. But God loved His people, and He had a plan.

key: God sent Moses and his brother Aaron to see the king. Moses said, "God says, let my people go!"
say: God sent Moses and his brother Aaron to see the king. Moses said, "God says, let my people go!"

key: Pharaoh said no, and no, and no again. But at last he said, "Go!" So off they went! God led the way, with a tall cloud in the day and a pillar of fire at night.
say: Pharaoh said no, and no, and no again. But at last he said, "Go!" So off they went! God led the way, with a tall cloud in the day and a pillar of fire at night.

key: They came to the edge of the Red Sea. But then Pharaoh changed his mind! Far away, his chariots were coming. Moses said, "Do not be afraid. God will help us!"
say: They came to the edge of the Red Sea. But then Pharaoh changed his mind! Far away, his chariots were coming. Moses said, "Do not be afraid. God will help us!"

key: Moses held out his staff over the sea. God sent a strong wind that blew all night long. Whoosh! The sea opened up, and the water stood up like two tall walls!
say: Moses held out his staff over the sea. God sent a strong wind that blew all night long. Whoosh! The sea opened up, and the water stood up like two tall walls!

key: Then God's people walked right through the sea on dry ground! Moms and dads, boys and girls, grandmas and grandpas, and even the sheep and goats.
say: Then God's people walked right through the sea on dry ground! Moms and dads, boys and girls, grandmas and grandpas, and even the sheep and goats.

key: God Makes a Way. God's people were walking through the sea on dry ground. Step by step, everyone made it all the way to the other side, safe and sound!
say: God Makes a Way. God's people were walking through the sea on dry ground. Step by step, everyone made it all the way to the other side, safe and sound!

key: Then Moses held out his hand over the sea, and the water came rushing back together. Splash! Now Pharaoh's chariots could not follow them.
say: Then Moses held out his hand over the sea, and the water came rushing back together. Splash! Now Pharaoh's chariots could not follow them.

key: God's people were safe and free! They would never have to make bricks for Pharaoh again. God had saved them!
say: God's people were safe and free! They would never have to make bricks for Pharaoh again. God had saved them!

key: Then Miriam, the big sister of Moses, picked up her tambourine. Jingle, jingle! The women danced, and everyone sang a happy song to God.
say: Then Miriam, the big sister of Moses, picked up her tambourine. Jingle, jingle! The women danced, and everyone sang a happy song to God.

key: God made a way for His people, right through the sea! And God is with you, too. He loves you, and He will always help you.
say: God made a way for His people, right through the sea! And God is with you, too. He loves you, and He will always help you.

key: Your way was through the sea. Psalm 77:19.
say: Your way was through the sea. Psalm seventy-seven, nineteen.

key: Daniel Loves to Pray. Long ago, there was a man named Daniel. God loved Daniel, and Daniel loved God with all his heart. Three times every day, he knelt by his open window and prayed to God.
say: Daniel Loves to Pray. Long ago, there was a man named Daniel. God loved Daniel, and Daniel loved God with all his heart. Three times every day, he knelt by his open window and prayed to God.

key: King Darius liked Daniel very much. Daniel was wise and kind, and he always told the truth. So the king gave him a very important job.
say: King Darius liked Daniel very much. Daniel was wise and kind, and he always told the truth. So the king gave him a very important job.

key: But some men were jealous of Daniel. They tricked the king. They said, "Make a new rule! For thirty days, everyone must pray only to you, or go into the lions' den." So the king signed the rule.
say: But some men were jealous of Daniel. They tricked the king. They said, "Make a new rule! For thirty days, everyone must pray only to you, or go into the lions' den." So the king signed the rule.

key: Daniel heard about the rule. But he still knelt by his open window and prayed to God, just like he always did. The jealous men saw him praying!
say: Daniel heard about the rule. But he still knelt by his open window and prayed to God, just like he always did. The jealous men saw him praying!

key: They hurried to tell the king. The king was very sad, because he loved Daniel. He tried and tried to help him. But the king's rule could not be changed.
say: They hurried to tell the king. The king was very sad, because he loved Daniel. He tried and tried to help him. But the king's rule could not be changed.

key: So Daniel was put into a den of lions, and a big stone was rolled over the door. The king said, "Daniel, your God will keep you safe!"
say: So Daniel was put into a den of lions, and a big stone was rolled over the door. The king said, "Daniel, your God will keep you safe!"

key: Safe All Night Long. That night, Daniel was in the lions' den. Back at the palace, the king could not sleep. He did not want to eat. He was so worried about Daniel.
say: Safe All Night Long. That night, Daniel was in the lions' den. Back at the palace, the king could not sleep. He did not want to eat. He was so worried about Daniel.

key: Early in the morning, the king hurried to the den. He called out, "Daniel! Did your God keep you safe from the lions?"
say: Early in the morning, the king hurried to the den. He called out, "Daniel! Did your God keep you safe from the lions?"

key: Daniel called back, "Yes, King Darius! My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They did not hurt me at all!"
say: Daniel called back, "Yes, King Darius! My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They did not hurt me at all!"

key: The king was so happy! He had the stone rolled away, and Daniel came out of the den. He did not have a single scratch, because he trusted God.
say: The king was so happy! He had the stone rolled away, and Daniel came out of the den. He did not have a single scratch, because he trusted God.

key: Then the king sent a letter to everyone in the land. It said, "Daniel's God is the living God! He saves, and He rescues."
say: Then the king sent a letter to everyone in the land. It said, "Daniel's God is the living God! He saves, and He rescues."

key: Daniel kept on praying every day, and God was always with him. You can talk to God any time, too, in the morning, at lunch, and at night. God always hears you!
say: Daniel kept on praying every day, and God was always with him. You can talk to God any time, too, in the morning, at lunch, and at night. God always hears you!

key: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths. Daniel 6:22.
say: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths. Daniel six, twenty-two.

key: A Basket in the Reeds. Long ago, God's people lived in the land of Egypt. God blessed them, and their family grew and grew. Soon they were a big, big family!
say: A Basket in the Reeds. Long ago, God's people lived in the land of Egypt. God blessed them, and their family grew and grew. Soon they were a big, big family!

key: Then a new king called Pharaoh was afraid of them, because there were so many. So he made God's people work very hard, making bricks all day long.
say: Then a new king called Pharaoh was afraid of them, because there were so many. So he made God's people work very hard, making bricks all day long.

key: Then Pharaoh made an unkind rule, and baby boys were not safe anymore. But God was watching over His people. And God had a plan!
say: Then Pharaoh made an unkind rule, and baby boys were not safe anymore. But God was watching over His people. And God had a plan!

key: One mom from God's people had a baby boy. He was a beautiful baby! His mom hid him at home and kept him safe for three whole months.
say: One mom from God's people had a baby boy. He was a beautiful baby! His mom hid him at home and kept him safe for three whole months.

key: When he got too big to hide, his mom made a little basket out of reeds. She coated it so no water could get in. Then she tucked her baby inside, snug and safe.
say: When he got too big to hide, his mom made a little basket out of reeds. She coated it so no water could get in. Then she tucked her baby inside, snug and safe.

key: She set the basket in the tall reeds by the river Nile. And his big sister Miriam hid nearby, to watch over him.
say: She set the basket in the tall reeds by the river Nile. And his big sister Miriam hid nearby, to watch over him.

key: The Princess and the Baby. The little basket floated in the reeds, and Miriam watched. Then Pharaoh's daughter, the princess, came down to the river to wash. She saw the basket, and she sent her helper to bring it to her.
say: The Princess and the Baby. The little basket floated in the reeds, and Miriam watched. Then Pharaoh's daughter, the princess, came down to the river to wash. She saw the basket, and she sent her helper to bring it to her.

key: The princess opened the basket. There was a baby boy, and he was crying! Waah! The princess felt so kind and loving toward him.
say: The princess opened the basket. There was a baby boy, and he was crying! Waah! The princess felt so kind and loving toward him.

key: Miriam ran up and asked, "Shall I find someone to take care of the baby for you?" "Yes, go!" said the princess. So Miriam ran and brought the baby's very own mom!
say: Miriam ran up and asked, "Shall I find someone to take care of the baby for you?" "Yes, go!" said the princess. So Miriam ran and brought the baby's very own mom!

key: The princess said, "Please take care of this baby for me." So his mom took her baby home again! She took care of him until he was bigger.
say: The princess said, "Please take care of this baby for me." So his mom took her baby home again! She took care of him until he was bigger.

key: When he was older, he went to live with the princess, and she named him Moses. She said, "I pulled him out of the water."
say: When he was older, he went to live with the princess, and she named him Moses. She said, "I pulled him out of the water."

key: God kept baby Moses safe, and God had a big plan for him! And God takes care of you, too. He loves you so much.
say: God kept baby Moses safe, and God had a big plan for him! And God takes care of you, too. He loves you so much.

key: Don't you be afraid, for I am with you. Isaiah 41:10.
say: Don't you be afraid, for I am with you. Isaiah forty-one, ten.

key: Moses the Shepherd. Baby Moses grew up in the palace of the king of Egypt. But Moses loved God's people. He was sad to see them work so hard, making bricks all day long.
say: Moses the Shepherd. Baby Moses grew up in the palace of the king of Egypt. But Moses loved God's people. He was sad to see them work so hard, making bricks all day long.

key: One day, Moses had to leave Egypt. He walked far, far away, across the hot desert, to a land called Midian.
say: One day, Moses had to leave Egypt. He walked far, far away, across the hot desert, to a land called Midian.

key: In Midian, Moses sat down by a well. Seven sisters came to give their sheep a drink. But some grumpy shepherds pushed them away. That was not kind!
say: In Midian, Moses sat down by a well. Seven sisters came to give their sheep a drink. But some grumpy shepherds pushed them away. That was not kind!

key: So Moses stood up and helped the sisters! He pulled up water from the well and filled the trough. All their thirsty sheep had a drink. Slurp, slurp!
say: So Moses stood up and helped the sisters! He pulled up water from the well and filled the trough. All their thirsty sheep had a drink. Slurp, slurp!

key: The sisters told their father, Jethro, all about kind Moses. Jethro said, "Come and live with us!" Moses married Zipporah, one of the sisters. And he became a shepherd.
say: The sisters told their father, Jethro, all about kind Moses. Jethro said, "Come and live with us!" Moses married Zipporah, one of the sisters. And he became a shepherd.

key: Moses took good care of Jethro's sheep. One day, he led them far across the desert, all the way to the mountain of God.
say: Moses took good care of Jethro's sheep. One day, he led them far across the desert, all the way to the mountain of God.

key: God Calls Moses. Moses was with his sheep by the mountain of God. Then he saw something very strange. A bush was on fire, but it did not burn up!
say: God Calls Moses. Moses was with his sheep by the mountain of God. Then he saw something very strange. A bush was on fire, but it did not burn up!

key: Moses said, "I will go closer and see!" Then God called to him from the bush, "Moses! Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am!"
say: Moses said, "I will go closer and see!" Then God called to him from the bush, "Moses! Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am!"

key: God said, "Take off your sandals, for this is holy ground." It was a special place, because God was there! So Moses took off his sandals.
say: God said, "Take off your sandals, for this is holy ground." It was a special place, because God was there! So Moses took off his sandals.

key: God said, "I have seen how hard My people work in Egypt, and I care about them. I will send you to Pharaoh, to bring My people out of Egypt."
say: God said, "I have seen how hard My people work in Egypt, and I care about them. I will send you to Pharaoh, to bring My people out of Egypt."

key: But Moses was afraid. "Who am I?" he said. "I can't do it!" God said, "I will be with you. And your brother Aaron will help you."
say: But Moses was afraid. "Who am I?" he said. "I can't do it!" God said, "I will be with you. And your brother Aaron will help you."

key: Moses trusted God. He took his staff and set off for Egypt, and Aaron came to meet him on the way. God was with Moses, and God is with you, too, even when you are afraid!
say: Moses trusted God. He took his staff and set off for Egypt, and Aaron came to meet him on the way. God was with Moses, and God is with you, too, even when you are afraid!

key: Certainly I will be with you. Exodus 3:12.
say: Certainly I will be with you. Exodus three, twelve.

key: Bread from Heaven. After God brought His people safely through the Red Sea, they walked on into the desert. Moses led the way, and God's tall cloud showed them where to go.
say: Bread from Heaven. After God brought His people safely through the Red Sea, they walked on into the desert. Moses led the way, and God's tall cloud showed them where to go.

key: The desert was hot and dry, and soon all the food was gone. Tummies rumbled, and the people grumbled. "We are hungry! In Egypt, we had bread to eat!"
say: The desert was hot and dry, and soon all the food was gone. Tummies rumbled, and the people grumbled. "We are hungry! In Egypt, we had bread to eat!"

key: God heard all that grumbling. But He still loved His people! God said to Moses, "I will rain bread from the sky for you!"
say: God heard all that grumbling. But He still loved His people! God said to Moses, "I will rain bread from the sky for you!"

key: That evening, God sent quail, lots and lots of little birds! They covered the whole camp. Now there was plenty of food for everyone.
say: That evening, God sent quail, lots and lots of little birds! They covered the whole camp. Now there was plenty of food for everyone.

key: The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes, like frost. Everyone came out of their tents to look. "What is it?" they said.
say: The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes, like frost. Everyone came out of their tents to look. "What is it?" they said.

key: Moses said, "It is the bread God has given you. Gather just enough for today." They called it manna. It tasted like crackers made with honey. Yum!
say: Moses said, "It is the bread God has given you. Gather just enough for today." They called it manna. It tasted like crackers made with honey. Yum!

key: Just Enough. God sent manna every morning, and He said, "Gather just enough for today." But some people saved extra, just in case. The next morning, it was spoiled and smelly! Pee-yew!
say: Just Enough. God sent manna every morning, and He said, "Gather just enough for today." But some people saved extra, just in case. The next morning, it was spoiled and smelly! Pee-yew!

key: But every morning, there was fresh manna on the ground again. Some people gathered a lot, and some gathered a little. And everyone had just enough!
say: But every morning, there was fresh manna on the ground again. Some people gathered a lot, and some gathered a little. And everyone had just enough!

key: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much. Then on the seventh day, everyone rested, and the saved manna stayed fresh and yummy!
say: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much. Then on the seventh day, everyone rested, and the saved manna stayed fresh and yummy!

key: One day, there was no water, and everyone was thirsty. God told Moses to hit a big rock with his staff. Moses did, and splash! Fresh water came pouring out!
say: One day, there was no water, and everyone was thirsty. God told Moses to hit a big rock with his staff. Moses did, and splash! Fresh water came pouring out!

key: For forty years, God fed His people with manna, every single day. Aaron even kept some manna in a jar, so they would always remember how God took care of them.
say: For forty years, God fed His people with manna, every single day. Aaron even kept some manna in a jar, so they would always remember how God took care of them.

key: God gave His people just what they needed, every single day. And God takes care of you, too! He loves you, and He gives you what you need, every day.
say: God gave His people just what they needed, every single day. And God takes care of you, too! He loves you, and He gives you what you need, every day.

key: Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you. Exodus 16:4.
say: Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you. Exodus sixteen, four.

key: The Walls of Jericho. Moses had led God's people for a long, long time. When he was very, very old, Moses went to be with God. Then God chose a new leader: Joshua! God said, "Be strong and brave! I will be with you wherever you go."
say: The Walls of Jericho. Moses had led God's people for a long, long time. When he was very, very old, Moses went to be with God. Then God chose a new leader: Joshua! God said, "Be strong and brave! I will be with you wherever you go."

key: Across the Jordan River was a city called Jericho. It had great big, strong walls all the way around. Joshua sent two men to go and look at it.
say: Across the Jordan River was a city called Jericho. It had great big, strong walls all the way around. Joshua sent two men to go and look at it.

key: In Jericho lived a kind woman named Rahab. Her house was built right into the big wall! She hid the two men up on her roof, to keep them safe.
say: In Jericho lived a kind woman named Rahab. Her house was built right into the big wall! She hid the two men up on her roof, to keep them safe.

key: Rahab said, "I know your God is the real God. Please keep my family safe!" The men said, "Tie this red cord in your window, and everyone in your house will be safe."
say: Rahab said, "I know your God is the real God. Please keep my family safe!" The men said, "Tie this red cord in your window, and everyone in your house will be safe."

key: Then God's people came to the Jordan River. When the priests carried God's special golden box into the water, God stopped the river! Everyone walked across on dry ground.
say: Then God's people came to the Jordan River. When the priests carried God's special golden box into the water, God stopped the river! Everyone walked across on dry ground.

key: God gave Joshua a strange plan. "March around Jericho once a day for six days. The priests will blow trumpets made from rams' horns. Everyone else must be very quiet."
say: God gave Joshua a strange plan. "March around Jericho once a day for six days. The priests will blow trumpets made from rams' horns. Everyone else must be very quiet."

key: Seven Times Around. Remember God's strange plan? Joshua and God's people did just what God said. They marched around Jericho one time. Toot, toot went the trumpets! Nobody else made a sound.
say: Seven Times Around. Remember God's strange plan? Joshua and God's people did just what God said. They marched around Jericho one time. Toot, toot went the trumpets! Nobody else made a sound.

key: The next day, they did it again. And the next day, and the next! Day after day, for six days, they marched around the city, just like God said.
say: The next day, they did it again. And the next day, and the next! Day after day, for six days, they marched around the city, just like God said.

key: On the seventh day, they marched around Jericho seven times! Then the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua said, "Shout! God has given you the city!"
say: On the seventh day, they marched around Jericho seven times! Then the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua said, "Shout! God has given you the city!"

key: So everybody shouted, as loud as they could. And the great big walls came tumbling down, flat on the ground! Crash!
say: So everybody shouted, as loud as they could. And the great big walls came tumbling down, flat on the ground! Crash!

key: But Rahab's house, with the red cord in the window, was safe. The two men brought Rahab and all her family out, safe and sound, just as they promised.
say: But Rahab's house, with the red cord in the window, was safe. The two men brought Rahab and all her family out, safe and sound, just as they promised.

key: Everyone thanked God. God was with Joshua, just as He promised. God always keeps His promises, and He is with you, too!
say: Everyone thanked God. God was with Joshua, just as He promised. God always keeps His promises, and He is with you, too!

key: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down. Hebrews 11:30.
say: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down. Hebrews eleven, thirty.

key: Ruth and Naomi. Long ago, a woman named Naomi lived in Bethlehem with her husband and their two boys. One year, there was no food in Bethlehem. So they moved far away, to a land called Moab.
say: Ruth and Naomi. Long ago, a woman named Naomi lived in Bethlehem with her husband and their two boys. One year, there was no food in Bethlehem. So they moved far away, to a land called Moab.

key: In Moab, the boys grew up. They married two kind women named Ruth and Orpah. Naomi loved Ruth and Orpah, and they loved her, too.
say: In Moab, the boys grew up. They married two kind women named Ruth and Orpah. Naomi loved Ruth and Orpah, and they loved her, too.

key: Then Naomi's husband and her two sons died, and she was very sad. One day, Naomi heard good news. God had given His people food in Bethlehem again! "I will go home," she said.
say: Then Naomi's husband and her two sons died, and she was very sad. One day, Naomi heard good news. God had given His people food in Bethlehem again! "I will go home," she said.

key: So Naomi set off for home, and Ruth and Orpah went with her. On the way, Naomi said, "Go back home to your mothers, my dears." Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye, and she went back home.
say: So Naomi set off for home, and Ruth and Orpah went with her. On the way, Naomi said, "Go back home to your mothers, my dears." Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye, and she went back home.

key: But Ruth hugged Naomi tight. "Where you go, I will go," said Ruth. "Your people will be my people, and your God my God."
say: But Ruth hugged Naomi tight. "Where you go, I will go," said Ruth. "Your people will be my people, and your God my God."

key: Ruth and Naomi walked together, all the way to Bethlehem. When they got there, the barley in the fields was golden and ready to harvest!
say: Ruth and Naomi walked together, all the way to Bethlehem. When they got there, the barley in the fields was golden and ready to harvest!

key: Kind Boaz. Remember Ruth and Naomi? They were home in Bethlehem, but they had no food. So Ruth went to pick up the leftover barley in a field. The field belonged to a kind man named Boaz.
say: Kind Boaz. Remember Ruth and Naomi? They were home in Bethlehem, but they had no food. So Ruth went to pick up the leftover barley in a field. The field belonged to a kind man named Boaz.

key: At lunchtime, Boaz shared his bread with Ruth, and cool water, too. Then he told his workers, "Drop some extra barley for her, on purpose!"
say: At lunchtime, Boaz shared his bread with Ruth, and cool water, too. Then he told his workers, "Drop some extra barley for her, on purpose!"

key: That evening, Ruth brought home a big basket full of barley! Naomi was so happy. "God bless kind Boaz!" she said. "God is taking care of us."
say: That evening, Ruth brought home a big basket full of barley! Naomi was so happy. "God bless kind Boaz!" she said. "God is taking care of us."

key: Boaz loved Ruth, and Ruth loved Boaz. So they got married! Everyone in Bethlehem was happy for them.
say: Boaz loved Ruth, and Ruth loved Boaz. So they got married! Everyone in Bethlehem was happy for them.

key: Then God gave Ruth and Boaz a baby boy named Obed. Naomi held baby Obed close. She was so happy again!
say: Then God gave Ruth and Boaz a baby boy named Obed. Naomi held baby Obed close. She was so happy again!

key: Baby Obed grew up, and one day he became the grandpa of King David! God took care of Ruth and Naomi, and God takes care of you, too.
say: Baby Obed grew up, and one day he became the grandpa of King David! God took care of Ruth and Naomi, and God takes care of you, too.

key: Your people will be my people, and your God my God. Ruth 1:16.
say: Your people will be my people, and your God my God. Ruth one, sixteen.

key: Hannah's Prayer. Long ago, there was a woman named Hannah. She wanted a baby very much, and she felt sad. One day at God's house, she prayed and prayed. "Please, God, give me a baby boy. He will be Your helper all his life."
say: Hannah's Prayer. Long ago, there was a woman named Hannah. She wanted a baby very much, and she felt sad. One day at God's house, she prayed and prayed. "Please, God, give me a baby boy. He will be Your helper all his life."

key: Old Eli the priest saw Hannah praying. He said, "Go in peace. May God give you what you asked for." And Hannah was not sad anymore.
say: Old Eli the priest saw Hannah praying. He said, "Go in peace. May God give you what you asked for." And Hannah was not sad anymore.

key: God heard Hannah's prayer! Soon she had a baby boy. She named him Samuel, because she said, "I asked God for him."
say: God heard Hannah's prayer! Soon she had a baby boy. She named him Samuel, because she said, "I asked God for him."

key: When Samuel was old enough, Hannah kept her promise. She brought him to God's house, to help old Eli and learn all about God.
say: When Samuel was old enough, Hannah kept her promise. She brought him to God's house, to help old Eli and learn all about God.

key: Samuel helped Eli in God's house. Every year, Hannah came to visit. She brought him a new little coat she had made, just his size!
say: Samuel helped Eli in God's house. Every year, Hannah came to visit. She brought him a new little coat she had made, just his size!

key: One night, God's lamp was still glowing, and Samuel was fast asleep in God's house. Then he heard someone call, "Samuel!"
say: One night, God's lamp was still glowing, and Samuel was fast asleep in God's house. Then he heard someone call, "Samuel!"

key: Here I Am. In the night, Samuel heard someone call his name. He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am! You called me." But Eli said, "I did not call you. Go back to bed."
say: Here I Am. In the night, Samuel heard someone call his name. He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am! You called me." But Eli said, "I did not call you. Go back to bed."

key: So Samuel lay down again. Then he heard it again: "Samuel!" He ran to Eli. "Here I am!" But Eli said, "I did not call you, my son. Lie down again."
say: So Samuel lay down again. Then he heard it again: "Samuel!" He ran to Eli. "Here I am!" But Eli said, "I did not call you, my son. Lie down again."

key: Then it happened a third time! Now Eli understood. God was calling Samuel! Eli said, "Go and lie down. If He calls you, say: Speak, Lord. I am listening."
say: Then it happened a third time! Now Eli understood. God was calling Samuel! Eli said, "Go and lie down. If He calls you, say: Speak, Lord. I am listening."

key: Samuel lay down. Then God came and called, just like before: "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, Lord. I am listening."
say: Samuel lay down. Then God came and called, just like before: "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, Lord. I am listening."

key: God spoke to Samuel, and Samuel listened. Samuel grew up, and God was with him. He told everyone what God said.
say: God spoke to Samuel, and Samuel listened. Samuel grew up, and God was with him. He told everyone what God said.

key: God hears us when we pray, just like He heard Hannah. And God speaks to us in the Bible. So let's listen to God, just like Samuel!
say: God hears us when we pray, just like He heard Hannah. And God speaks to us in the Bible. So let's listen to God, just like Samuel!

key: Speak; for your servant hears. 1 Samuel 3:10.
say: Speak; for your servant hears. First Samuel three, ten.

key: God Takes Care of Elijah. Long ago, a man named Elijah loved God. But King Ahab and many of God's people forgot about God. So Elijah told the king, "There will be no rain, not one drop, until God says so!"
say: God Takes Care of Elijah. Long ago, a man named Elijah loved God. But King Ahab and many of God's people forgot about God. So Elijah told the king, "There will be no rain, not one drop, until God says so!"

key: And no rain fell, for a long, dry time. The grass turned brown, and the ground cracked. But God took care of Elijah. He said, "Go and stay by the little brook. You can drink its water."
say: And no rain fell, for a long, dry time. The grass turned brown, and the ground cracked. But God took care of Elijah. He said, "Go and stay by the little brook. You can drink its water."

key: Every morning and every evening, God sent ravens to Elijah. Flap, flap! The big black birds brought him bread and meat to eat. And Elijah drank water from the brook.
say: Every morning and every evening, God sent ravens to Elijah. Flap, flap! The big black birds brought him bread and meat to eat. And Elijah drank water from the brook.

key: After a while, the little brook dried up. Then God said, "Go to a town far away. A widow there will give you food."
say: After a while, the little brook dried up. Then God said, "Go to a town far away. A widow there will give you food."

key: At the town gate, the widow and her little boy were picking up sticks. "Please, may I have a little bread?" Elijah asked. She said, "I only have enough flour and oil for one last loaf."
say: At the town gate, the widow and her little boy were picking up sticks. "Please, may I have a little bread?" Elijah asked. She said, "I only have enough flour and oil for one last loaf."

key: "Don't be afraid," said Elijah. "God will not let your flour and oil run out." So the widow shared her bread. And God made her flour and oil last and last, for all three of them!
say: "Don't be afraid," said Elijah. "God will not let your flour and oil run out." So the widow shared her bread. And God made her flour and oil last and last, for all three of them!

key: Fire from Heaven. Remember? There was still no rain. Elijah called all the people to Mount Carmel. "Let's see who the real God is!" he said. Some people prayed to a pretend god, all day long. But nothing happened.
say: Fire from Heaven. Remember? There was still no rain. Elijah called all the people to Mount Carmel. "Let's see who the real God is!" he said. Some people prayed to a pretend god, all day long. But nothing happened.

key: Then Elijah built an altar to God with twelve big stones. He put wood on top and dug a ditch around it. "Pour water all over it!" he said. Splash, splash! The water filled the ditch.
say: Then Elijah built an altar to God with twelve big stones. He put wood on top and dug a ditch around it. "Pour water all over it!" he said. Splash, splash! The water filled the ditch.

key: Elijah prayed, "Lord, show everyone that You are God." Whoosh! God sent fire from heaven! It burned up the wood and the stones, and even all the water!
say: Elijah prayed, "Lord, show everyone that You are God." Whoosh! God sent fire from heaven! It burned up the wood and the stones, and even all the water!

key: When the people saw it, they knelt down and said, "The Lord is God! The Lord is God!" Even the people who had prayed to the pretend god knew it now.
say: When the people saw it, they knelt down and said, "The Lord is God! The Lord is God!" Even the people who had prayed to the pretend god knew it now.

key: Then Elijah prayed for rain. He prayed and prayed. At last, far out over the sea, a little cloud came up, as small as a hand.
say: Then Elijah prayed for rain. He prayed and prayed. At last, far out over the sea, a little cloud came up, as small as a hand.

key: The little cloud grew and grew, and the sky turned dark. Then down came the rain! Splish, splash! The thirsty land drank and drank. God answers prayer, and God takes care of His people.
say: The little cloud grew and grew, and the sky turned dark. Then down came the rain! Splish, splash! The thirsty land drank and drank. God answers prayer, and God takes care of His people.

key: My God will supply every need of yours. Philippians 4:19.
say: My God will supply every need of yours. Philippians four, nineteen.

key: Esther Becomes Queen. Long ago, there was a girl named Esther. She had no mom or dad, so her big cousin Mordecai took care of her. He loved her like his very own daughter.
say: Esther Becomes Queen. Long ago, there was a girl named Esther. She had no mom or dad, so her big cousin Mordecai took care of her. He loved her like his very own daughter.

key: Esther grew up to be kind and lovely. King Xerxes chose Esther to be his queen! He put a royal crown on her head.
say: Esther grew up to be kind and lovely. King Xerxes chose Esther to be his queen! He put a royal crown on her head.

key: Mordecai worked at the king's gate. One day, he heard two men whispering a plan to hurt the king. He told Queen Esther, and she told the king. Good Mordecai saved the king!
say: Mordecai worked at the king's gate. One day, he heard two men whispering a plan to hurt the king. He told Queen Esther, and she told the king. Good Mordecai saved the king!

key: There was a proud man named Haman. He wanted everyone to bow down to him. Everybody did, but not Mordecai! Mordecai bowed down only to God.
say: There was a proud man named Haman. He wanted everyone to bow down to him. Everybody did, but not Mordecai! Mordecai bowed down only to God.

key: Haman was so cross that he made a mean plan against Mordecai and all of God's people. Mordecai was very sad. He sent a message to Queen Esther: "Please ask the king to help us!"
say: Haman was so cross that he made a mean plan against Mordecai and all of God's people. Mordecai was very sad. He sent a message to Queen Esther: "Please ask the king to help us!"

key: Esther read the message, and she was afraid. No one could go to see the king unless he called them! But maybe God made Esther queen for a time just like this.
say: Esther read the message, and she was afraid. No one could go to see the king unless he called them! But maybe God made Esther queen for a time just like this.

key: Brave Queen Esther. Esther was afraid to go and see the king. So she asked God's people to pray for her. For three days, Esther and her friends prayed to God, too.
say: Brave Queen Esther. Esther was afraid to go and see the king. So she asked God's people to pray for her. For three days, Esther and her friends prayed to God, too.

key: On the third day, brave Queen Esther went to see the king. Would he be cross? No! He held out his golden scepter. That meant, "Come in!"
say: On the third day, brave Queen Esther went to see the king. Would he be cross? No! He held out his golden scepter. That meant, "Come in!"

key: The king asked, "What would you like, Queen Esther?" Esther said, "Please come to my dinner, and bring Haman, too." What a yummy dinner! Then she asked them to come back for another one.
say: The king asked, "What would you like, Queen Esther?" Esther said, "Please come to my dinner, and bring Haman, too." What a yummy dinner! Then she asked them to come back for another one.

key: At the next dinner, Esther told the king the truth. "Haman made a mean plan against my people, God's people. Please save us!"
say: At the next dinner, Esther told the king the truth. "Haman made a mean plan against my people, God's people. Please save us!"

key: The king listened to Queen Esther. He made a new rule to keep God's people safe, and he made good Mordecai his top helper. God's people were saved! Hooray!
say: The king listened to Queen Esther. He made a new rule to keep God's people safe, and he made good Mordecai his top helper. God's people were saved! Hooray!

key: God's people had a great big happy party, called Purim! They shared yummy food and gave presents. God took care of His people all along, and He takes care of you, too!
say: God's people had a great big happy party, called Purim! They shared yummy food and gave presents. God took care of His people all along, and He takes care of you, too!

key: Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid. Joshua 1:9.
say: Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid. Joshua one, nine.

key: Off to Jerusalem. Jesus grew up in a little town called Nazareth, with Mary and Joseph. Every year, Mary and Joseph went to Jerusalem for a big, happy feast called the Passover.
say: Off to Jerusalem. Jesus grew up in a little town called Nazareth, with Mary and Joseph. Every year, Mary and Joseph went to Jerusalem for a big, happy feast called the Passover.

key: When Jesus was twelve years old, He went too! Lots of family and friends walked together. It was a long way, so they sang happy songs on the road.
say: When Jesus was twelve years old, He went too! Lots of family and friends walked together. It was a long way, so they sang happy songs on the road.

key: At last, they saw Jerusalem, up on its hill. And there was God's house, the temple, shining in the sun!
say: At last, they saw Jerusalem, up on its hill. And there was God's house, the temple, shining in the sun!

key: The city was busy, busy, busy! People came from near and far for the feast. Jesus and His family went to God's house, to pray and to praise God.
say: The city was busy, busy, busy! People came from near and far for the feast. Jesus and His family went to God's house, to pray and to praise God.

key: Then they ate the Passover dinner together. They ate flat bread, and they remembered how God set His people free from Egypt, long ago.
say: Then they ate the Passover dinner together. They ate flat bread, and they remembered how God set His people free from Egypt, long ago.

key: When the feast was over, everyone set off for home, walking and talking together. But Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and Mary and Joseph didn't know!
say: When the feast was over, everyone set off for home, walking and talking together. But Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and Mary and Joseph didn't know!

key: In My Father's House. Everyone was walking home from the feast. That evening, Mary and Joseph looked for Jesus. Was He with their family? Was He with their friends? No, Jesus wasn't there!
say: In My Father's House. Everyone was walking home from the feast. That evening, Mary and Joseph looked for Jesus. Was He with their family? Was He with their friends? No, Jesus wasn't there!

key: So Mary and Joseph hurried back to Jerusalem. They looked and looked for Jesus, all over the big, busy city.
say: So Mary and Joseph hurried back to Jerusalem. They looked and looked for Jesus, all over the big, busy city.

key: On the third day, they found Jesus in God's house! He was sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
say: On the third day, they found Jesus in God's house! He was sitting with the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.

key: Everyone who heard Jesus was amazed. He understood so much about God!
say: Everyone who heard Jesus was amazed. He understood so much about God!

key: Mary said, "Son, we were looking everywhere for You!" Jesus said, "Didn't you know I must be in My Father's house?" Jesus is God's Son, so God's house is His Father's house!
say: Mary said, "Son, we were looking everywhere for You!" Jesus said, "Didn't you know I must be in My Father's house?" Jesus is God's Son, so God's house is His Father's house!

key: Then Jesus went home to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph, and He obeyed them. Jesus grew bigger and wiser, and God and people loved Him. And God loves you, too!
say: Then Jesus went home to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph, and He obeyed them. Jesus grew bigger and wiser, and God and people loved Him. And God loves you, too!

key: I must be in my Father's house. Luke 2:49.
say: I must be in my Father's house. Luke two, forty-nine.

key: Fishers of People. One morning, Jesus was by the Lake of Galilee. A great big crowd came to hear Him talk about God.
say: Fishers of People. One morning, Jesus was by the Lake of Galilee. A great big crowd came to hear Him talk about God.

key: Two fishing boats sat on the shore. The fishermen were washing their nets. Their nets were empty. Not one fish!
say: Two fishing boats sat on the shore. The fishermen were washing their nets. Their nets were empty. Not one fish!

key: One boat belonged to a fisherman named Peter. His brother Andrew fished with him. Jesus got into Peter's boat, and they pushed it out onto the water. Then Jesus sat down and taught the people from the boat.
say: One boat belonged to a fisherman named Peter. His brother Andrew fished with him. Jesus got into Peter's boat, and they pushed it out onto the water. Then Jesus sat down and taught the people from the boat.

key: When Jesus was done teaching, He said to Peter, "Now go out where the water is deep, and let down your nets."
say: When Jesus was done teaching, He said to Peter, "Now go out where the water is deep, and let down your nets."

key: Peter said, "Teacher, we worked hard all night, and we didn't catch anything. But because You say so, I will!"
say: Peter said, "Teacher, we worked hard all night, and we didn't catch anything. But because You say so, I will!"

key: Come, Follow Me. Peter let down the nets, just like Jesus said. Then, splash! So many fish! The nets were so full, they started to break.
say: Come, Follow Me. Peter let down the nets, just like Jesus said. Then, splash! So many fish! The nets were so full, they started to break.

key: Peter waved to James and John in the other boat. "Come and help us!" Soon both boats were so full of fish, they sank down low in the water!
say: Peter waved to James and John in the other boat. "Come and help us!" Soon both boats were so full of fish, they sank down low in the water!

key: Peter knelt down in front of Jesus. He was amazed, and a little bit scared. Jesus smiled and said, "Don't be afraid. Come, follow Me, and I will make you fishers of people."
say: Peter knelt down in front of Jesus. He was amazed, and a little bit scared. Jesus smiled and said, "Don't be afraid. Come, follow Me, and I will make you fishers of people."

key: So they pulled their boats up onto the shore. They left everything, and they followed Jesus! James and John's dad, Zebedee, stayed in his boat with his helpers and waved goodbye.
say: So they pulled their boats up onto the shore. They left everything, and they followed Jesus! James and John's dad, Zebedee, stayed in his boat with his helpers and waved goodbye.

key: Now Peter and his friends were fishers of people. They helped everyone know how much God loves them! Jesus wants you to follow Him, too. And God loves you, every single day.
say: Now Peter and his friends were fishers of people. They helped everyone know how much God loves them! Jesus wants you to follow Him, too. And God loves you, every single day.

key: Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men. Matthew 4:19.
say: Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men. Matthew four, nineteen.

key: A Boat Ride with Jesus. One day, lots of people came to the big lake to hear Jesus. He sat in a boat near the shore, and He taught them all about God's love.
say: A Boat Ride with Jesus. One day, lots of people came to the big lake to hear Jesus. He sat in a boat near the shore, and He taught them all about God's love.

key: When evening came, Jesus said to His friends, "Let's go over to the other side of the lake." So they got the boat ready to go.
say: When evening came, Jesus said to His friends, "Let's go over to the other side of the lake." So they got the boat ready to go.

key: Off they sailed across the lake! The wind filled up the sail, and the boat went swish, swish over the water. Other little boats sailed along with them.
say: Off they sailed across the lake! The wind filled up the sail, and the boat went swish, swish over the water. Other little boats sailed along with them.

key: Jesus was very tired after His long day. He lay down at the back of the boat, put His head on a cushion, and fell fast asleep.
say: Jesus was very tired after His long day. He lay down at the back of the boat, put His head on a cushion, and fell fast asleep.

key: The boat sailed on and on. Then dark clouds rolled over the hills, and the wind began to blow. Whoosh! But Jesus was still fast asleep.
say: The boat sailed on and on. Then dark clouds rolled over the hills, and the wind began to blow. Whoosh! But Jesus was still fast asleep.

key: Jesus Calms the Storm. Remember the dark clouds? Soon a big storm came! The wind blew and blew, and big waves splashed into the boat. The boat began to fill up with water. But Jesus was still asleep!
say: Jesus Calms the Storm. Remember the dark clouds? Soon a big storm came! The wind blew and blew, and big waves splashed into the boat. The boat began to fill up with water. But Jesus was still asleep!

key: The friends were scared. They woke Jesus up and said, "Teacher, don't You care? We're sinking!"
say: The friends were scared. They woke Jesus up and said, "Teacher, don't You care? We're sinking!"

key: Jesus stood up. He said to the wind and the waves, "Peace! Be still!"
say: Jesus stood up. He said to the wind and the waves, "Peace! Be still!"

key: Right away, the wind stopped, and the waves went still. Everything was calm and quiet. The first little stars came out to twinkle.
say: Right away, the wind stopped, and the waves went still. Everything was calm and quiet. The first little stars came out to twinkle.

key: Jesus asked them gently, "Why were you so afraid? Do you still not trust Me?" His friends were amazed. "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey Him!"
say: Jesus asked them gently, "Why were you so afraid? Do you still not trust Me?" His friends were amazed. "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey Him!"

key: They all sailed safely to the other side. Who is Jesus? He is God's own Son! When we are scared, Jesus is with us, and He takes care of us.
say: They all sailed safely to the other side. Who is Jesus? He is God's own Son! When we are scared, Jesus is with us, and He takes care of us.

key: He makes the storm a calm,
say: He makes the storm a calm,

key: He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Psalm 107:29.
say: He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Psalm one hundred seven, twenty-nine.

key: The Lost Sheep. Jesus loved to tell stories, and all kinds of people came to listen. One day, Jesus told them this story.
say: The Lost Sheep. Jesus loved to tell stories, and all kinds of people came to listen. One day, Jesus told them this story.

key: There once was a shepherd who had one hundred sheep! Every day, he led them to green grass and cool water.
say: There once was a shepherd who had one hundred sheep! Every day, he led them to green grass and cool water.

key: The shepherd took good care of his sheep. He loved every one of them, even the littlest lamb.
say: The shepherd took good care of his sheep. He loved every one of them, even the littlest lamb.

key: Every evening, he counted his sheep into the sheepfold. One evening he counted: ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine. Oh no! One little lamb was missing!
say: Every evening, he counted his sheep into the sheepfold. One evening he counted: ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine. Oh no! One little lamb was missing!

key: The shepherd made sure his ninety-nine sheep were safe together. Then off he went, to look for his little lost lamb.
say: The shepherd made sure his ninety-nine sheep were safe together. Then off he went, to look for his little lost lamb.

key: The Lamb Comes Home. Remember the little lost lamb? The shepherd looked for it over the hills, behind the rocks, and through the bushes. "Little lamb! Where are you?" he called.
say: The Lamb Comes Home. Remember the little lost lamb? The shepherd looked for it over the hills, behind the rocks, and through the bushes. "Little lamb! Where are you?" he called.

key: Then he heard a little voice: "Baa! Baa!" There was the little lamb, stuck in a bush! It was a little bit scared, but it was not hurt.
say: Then he heard a little voice: "Baa! Baa!" There was the little lamb, stuck in a bush! It was a little bit scared, but it was not hurt.

key: The shepherd gently lifted the lamb out of the bush and put it on his shoulders. He was so happy! Then he carried it all the way home.
say: The shepherd gently lifted the lamb out of the bush and put it on his shoulders. He was so happy! Then he carried it all the way home.

key: He called his friends and neighbors: "Celebrate with me! I found my lost sheep!" And everyone was so happy.
say: He called his friends and neighbors: "Celebrate with me! I found my lost sheep!" And everyone was so happy.

key: Jesus said God is like that shepherd. God loves every one of us so much, and He always comes looking for us. When one of us comes home to God, heaven is full of joy!
say: Jesus said God is like that shepherd. God loves every one of us so much, and He always comes looking for us. When one of us comes home to God, heaven is full of joy!

key: Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost! Luke 15:6.
say: Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost! Luke fifteen, six.

key: The Good Samaritan. One day, a man asked Jesus a question. "God says to love my neighbor," he said. "But who is my neighbor?" So Jesus told him a story.
say: The Good Samaritan. One day, a man asked Jesus a question. "God says to love my neighbor," he said. "But who is my neighbor?" So Jesus told him a story.

key: A man was walking down a long, rocky road, from Jerusalem to Jericho. On the way, robbers took his things and left him hurt by the side of the road.
say: A man was walking down a long, rocky road, from Jerusalem to Jericho. On the way, robbers took his things and left him hurt by the side of the road.

key: Soon a priest came down the road. He saw the hurt man. But he did not stop. He went by on the other side of the road.
say: Soon a priest came down the road. He saw the hurt man. But he did not stop. He went by on the other side of the road.

key: Then a temple helper came by. He saw the hurt man, too. But he hurried by on the other side. Would anyone stop to help?
say: Then a temple helper came by. He saw the hurt man, too. But he hurried by on the other side. Would anyone stop to help?

key: Then a Samaritan, a man from Samaria, came by with his donkey. His people and the hurt man's people did not get along. But when he saw the hurt man, he stopped. He felt so sorry for him!
say: Then a Samaritan, a man from Samaria, came by with his donkey. His people and the hurt man's people did not get along. But when he saw the hurt man, he stopped. He felt so sorry for him!

key: The Samaritan gently washed the man's hurts and wrapped them in bandages. Then he lifted him up onto his own donkey.
say: The Samaritan gently washed the man's hurts and wrapped them in bandages. Then he lifted him up onto his own donkey.

key: A Good Neighbor. Remember the hurt man on the road? The kind Samaritan took him to an inn, a house where travelers can stay. The innkeeper opened the door. "Come in, come in!" he said.
say: A Good Neighbor. Remember the hurt man on the road? The kind Samaritan took him to an inn, a house where travelers can stay. The innkeeper opened the door. "Come in, come in!" he said.

key: That night, the Samaritan took care of him. He gave him water to drink and warm soup to eat, and he tucked him into a cozy bed.
say: That night, the Samaritan took care of him. He gave him water to drink and warm soup to eat, and he tucked him into a cozy bed.

key: In the morning, the Samaritan gave the innkeeper two coins. "Please take care of him," he said. "I will come back."
say: In the morning, the Samaritan gave the innkeeper two coins. "Please take care of him," he said. "I will come back."

key: Then Jesus asked, "Which one was a good neighbor to the hurt man?" The man said, "The one who was kind to him." "Yes," said Jesus. "Now you go and do the same."
say: Then Jesus asked, "Which one was a good neighbor to the hurt man?" The man said, "The one who was kind to him." "Yes," said Jesus. "Now you go and do the same."

key: A neighbor is anyone who needs our help. God loves everyone. He wants us to be kind to everyone, even people who are different from us, just like the good Samaritan!
say: A neighbor is anyone who needs our help. God loves everyone. He wants us to be kind to everyone, even people who are different from us, just like the good Samaritan!

key: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Matthew 22:39.
